questions.stem: Which area does an interscalene block cover besides the shoulder and upper arm?
options: Medial two thirds of the clavicle
Lateral two thirds of the clavicle

questions.stem: In an interscalene block, what else can proximal superficial spread block?
questions.answer: Supraclavicular branches of the cervical plexus

questions.stem: Which trunk of the brachial plexus is usually spared by an interscalene block?
For ulnar (C8-T1) territory with a low interscalene injection, what volume is used?
Which surgery is an interscalene block indicated for?
Which surgery is an interscalene block combined with a cervical plexus block for?
questions.answer: Clavicle surgery

questions.stem: Interscalene block ultrasound uses a linear transducer at ____ MHz.
For an interscalene block, which head position is used relative to the side being blocked?
options: Head turned toward the side to be blocked
Head flexed fully over the chest
Head turned away from the side to be blocked

questions.stem: In an interscalene block, what does a slight head-up tilt achieve?
questions.answer: More comfort, better venous drainage and less prominent neck veins

questions.stem: In an interscalene block, what does a pillow under the neck and contralateral shoulder achieve?
questions.answer: It lifts the site and gives more room posteriorly

questions.stem: In an interscalene block, what manoeuvre drops the shoulder?
questions.answer: Reaching for the ipsilateral knee

questions.stem: At which level is the linear probe placed transversely for an interscalene block?
options: At the angle of the jaw (C2)

questions.stem: For ultrasound interscalene block, the probe sits about ____ cm above the clavicle, over the external jugular vein.
In interscalene ultrasound, which structure do you find first before scanning laterally?
questions.answer: Carotid artery

questions.stem: On interscalene ultrasound, where does the plexus lie relative to the carotid and internal jugular vein?
questions.answer: Lateral to them, between anterior and middle scalenes

questions.stem: On interscalene ultrasound the brachial plexus is typically ____ cm deep.
What lies superficial to the plexus in the interscalene ultrasound view?
questions.answer: Sternocleidomastoid and the superficial cervical plexus

questions.stem: Which vessel should be avoided during an interscalene block?
At which vertebral level does the vertebral artery enter the transverse foramen, relevant to interscalene block?
Which nerve runs on the anterior scalene, relevant to interscalene block?
What is the name of the prominent anterior tubercle of the C6 transverse process?
questions.answer: Chassaignac tubercle

questions.stem: In traceback interscalene ultrasound, which vessel do you find first at the base of the neck?
questions.answer: Subclavian artery

questions.stem: If the interscalene view is hard to obtain, where should ultrasound scanning start?
questions.answer: Supraclavicular fossa

questions.stem: In interscalene block, from which direction is the needle usually advanced in-plane?
What sensation is often felt as the needle passes through the prevertebral fascia in interscalene block?
questions.answer: A pop

questions.stem: In interscalene block, where should the needle aim?
options: The space between anterior and middle scalenes, between roots

questions.stem: A ____ mL volume usually gives a fast, reliable interscalene block.
In interscalene block, why should high injection resistance be avoided?
questions.answer: Intraneural injection can track proximally into the spinal canal

questions.stem: What opening pressure suggests the needle is touching the plexus in interscalene block?
questions.answer: > 15 psi

questions.stem: Is a motor response required to confirm placement in an interscalene block?
questions.answer: No; it confirms placement but is not required

questions.stem: In interscalene block, what should you do if a motor response is seen below 0.5 mA?
questions.answer: Withdraw slightly before injecting

questions.stem: After what volume should spread be checked in an interscalene block?
questions.answer: 5–7 mL

questions.stem: After 10 mL in interscalene block, what is seen around the nerves lateral to the subclavian artery at the supraclavicular fossa?
questions.answer: The nerves are surrounded and look deeper

questions.stem: In interscalene block, where should you inject when C6 and C7 split proximally?
questions.answer: Between C5 and C6, superficial to C5 or deep to C6

questions.stem: If C5 runs partly through the anterior scalene, what should you do?
questions.answer: Follow it distally until it enters the groove

questions.stem: In the interscalene landmark technique, from which point do you draw a line laterally?
questions.answer: The cricoid

questions.stem: In the interscalene landmark technique, what do you palpate?
questions.answer: The interscalene groove

questions.stem: In the interscalene landmark technique the needle is usually only ____ cm deep.
How does a superior trunk block compare with an interscalene block for phrenic nerve involvement?
options: More distal, so further from the phrenic nerve
More proximal, so closer to the phrenic nerve
Equally close to the phrenic nerve
It always blocks the phrenic nerve

questions.stem: The suprascapular nerve supplies ____ of shoulder joint innervation and arises from the superior trunk.
During a superior trunk block, how do you locate the suprascapular nerve?
questions.answer: Slide the probe distally until it is seen leaving the superior trunk.

questions.stem: In a superior trunk block, how can you reach the superior trunk by following nerve roots?
questions.answer: Follow C5 and C6 caudally until they join, ideally above the suprascapular branch.

questions.stem: Which needle approach is used for a superior trunk block?
What volume is given when the needle tip is posterior or inferior to the superior trunk?
What volume is used when the tip is redirected anterior or superior, still lateral to the superior trunk?
Which respiratory complication follows ipsilateral phrenic nerve block during interscalene block?
With traditional volumes of 20 ml or more, how often does interscalene block cause hemidiaphragmatic paresis?
options: Occurs in about half of patients

questions.stem: With lower dose and volume, what incidence of hemidiaphragmatic paresis is reported after interscalene block?
Which sympathetic block complication of interscalene block causes ptosis, anhidrosis and miosis?
What can cause hoarseness after interscalene block?
questions.answer: Laryngeal hyperaemia or recurrent laryngeal nerve block.

questions.stem: What can an interscalene injection into a cervical root's dural sleeve cause?
questions.answer: Epidural spread or total spinal.

questions.stem: What complication follows accidental vertebral artery injection during interscalene block?
What is the risk of needle contact during interscalene block at the cervical level?
questions.answer: Direct needle injury to the cervical spinal cord.

questions.stem: Why does sitting position in shoulder surgery risk the Bezold-Jarisch reflex?
questions.answer: It reduces venous return, leading to bradycardia, hypotension and even cardiac arrest.

questions.stem: Where does the phrenic nerve lie relative to the interscalene groove at the cricoid level?
questions.answer: Just superficial to the groove, running over the anterior scalene.

questions.stem: Why does phrenic block after interscalene block matter for patients with lung disease?
questions.answer: It can compromise breathing in pre-existing lung disease.

questions.stem: How can phrenic block after interscalene block be checked with M-mode ultrasound?
questions.answer: Low-frequency curvilinear probe under the rib cage in the anterior axillary line, watching hemidiaphragm movement.

questions.stem: Which lower interscalene volume may give shorter analgesia and lower success?
In continuous interscalene block, how is catheter position confirmed after advancing the catheter?
questions.answer: Inject via the catheter under ultrasound.

questions.stem: In continuous interscalene block, which steps does ultrasound guide?
In continuous interscalene block, under which fascia does the needle usually lie?
questions.answer: Prevertebral fascia.

questions.stem: In continuous interscalene block, after a motor response at 0.5 mA and 0.1 msec, give ____ to open the space.
questions.answer: 4–5 mL

questions.stem: How far is the catheter advanced into the interscalene space in continuous interscalene block?
What can be injected to check an unclear catheter tip in continuous interscalene block?
When should tunnelling of an interscalene catheter be considered?
questions.answer: Older or obese patients, loose neck skin, or longer planned infusions.

questions.stem: Why can a stimulating catheter prompt needless manipulation in continuous interscalene block?
questions.answer: A motor response may be absent even when the catheter is well placed.

questions.stem: Which catheter technique has been reintroduced as an option for continuous interscalene block?
questions.answer: Catheter-over-needle technique.
